title: Doing something to one session
description: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/send, /interrupt and /close. Each has a precondition that is not the terminal's to check, so none of them is a thin wrapper over a keystroke.

force.description: Close although something is still owed. It cannot override an unreadable obligation list: overriding a refusal is a decision, and there is nothing to decide about when the list could not be read.

ActionResult.description: What actually happened. `typed` is the strongest thing a send can claim: the bytes reached the tty. Whether the assistant took the turn is a separate fact, read from the fleet list, and this never asserts it.

forced.description: Present on a close that went ahead over open obligations.

CloseRefusal.description: A close refused by what the session still owes. It carries the same reasons the fleet list was already showing, so the screen and the action never disagree.
